RXV2-0.9.152-ap-only-ux: Polishes the new 'AP mode only' option. (1) Plain-English explanation on the WiFi page — spells out that AP mode means the receiver makes its own little WiFi network your phone joins directly (no home router), why you'd tick it at the field, and that you'll need to switch your phone's WiFi after saving. (2) The save page no longer sits there waiting: when you turn AP-only on it stops polling the old address (which has gone) and instead clearly tells you to open your phone's WiFi settings, join the receiver's network (named), and go to 192.168.4.1. (3) Bug fix: the status page now shows the receiver's REAL access-point name (its model name, e.g. your renamed receiver) instead of always showing the old default 'LDRC_RX'.
RXV2-0.9.150-ap-only: Adds an 'AP mode only' tick-box to the WiFi page. When on, the receiver skips trying to join your home WiFi and comes straight up as its own access point — handy at the flying field, where the home network is miles away and the receiver would otherwise spend every boot fruitlessly retrying it. Your saved home SSID/password are kept; just untick it to use home WiFi again. The choice is saved in NVS and survives reboots/updates.
RXV2-0.9.149-wifi-advice: Adds a setup tip on the WiFi page (and its help): WiFi is steadiest with the transmitter switched off, because the control radio and WiFi share the 2.4GHz band and a live transmitter link can make WiFi drop in and out. Advises using the transmitter or the phone when you can — both together works fine, but expect WiFi to be less consistent. Text only; no behaviour change. (Includes the data/web files, so the page updates.)
RXV2-0.9.148-flash-fixed: FIXES the channels flashing to zero on the Configurator. Root cause, pinned down by on-board logging: whenever WiFi tried to reconnect — and WiFi drops a lot while flying because the radio desenses it — the reconnect ran inline and FROZE the main loop for ~208ms each attempt, long enough to pause RC output and starve the radio, so the flight-controller saw a brief RX-loss and the channels flashed to zero, then recovered. WiFi reconnection is now fully non-blocking: the loop never stalls and RC output stays continuous no matter how much WiFi flaps. Verified over 20+ minutes connected with WiFi flapping throughout — zero output stalls, zero spurious drops. (Also rolls up the supporting robustness work from 0.9.136-0.9.140: failsafe keyed off the real packet stream, a short board-ID burst then continuous telemetry like V1, gentler dual-radio failover, out-of-range frames rejected so the last good values are held, and no FC version-polling while a link is live.)
RXV2-0.9.140-no-fc-probe-flying: Found the real cause of the channels flashing to zero in the Rotorflight Configurator. The actual RC output was never glitching (steady 250Hz, link solid) — it was only the Configurator's *display*. The receiver was polling the flight-controller over MSP every few seconds to read its firmware version; that made the receiver a second MSP 'master' on the FC, colliding with the Configurator's own MSP polling of the same FC, so the Configurator periodically read an empty frame and showed all channels at zero. The receiver now never probes the FC while a transmitter link is live (it already behaved this way on shipping firmware; a dev-only setting was bypassing it). FC-version detection still happens when not flying, which is when the web page needs it. Note: the model itself was always controlled correctly throughout — this was a bench-display artifact, not a flight risk.
RXV2-0.9.139-hold-last-good: Channels flashing to zero, fixed the way V1 does it: hold the last good value. Two V1 behaviours the receiver was missing are now restored. (1) Crazy-value rejection: the transmitter periodically sends non-channel frames (bind/ID/parameter data); if one was misread as channel data it drove every channel to zero for an instant. Like V1's CheckForCrazyValues, any decoded frame with a channel outside the legal 500-2500us range is now rejected and the last good values are held. (2) The output no longer goes briefly silent on a momentary gap: the failsafe timeout is raised from 500ms to V1's 1500ms, and below it the receiver keeps streaming the held channel values (exactly as V1 keeps sending its SBUS frames) instead of detaching the CRSF line. True signal loss (>1.5s) still drops the link so the flight-controller can fail-safe.
RXV2-0.9.138-swap-storm-fix: The actual cause of the channels flashing to zero. When the active radio missed packets for a moment the receiver would try the other transceiver — correct — but it kept re-trying every 50ms in a tight storm (~20 swaps/second), and each swap briefly stops listening and reconfigures, which tore down the CRSF output stream long enough for the flight-controller to register a momentary RX-loss (the flash). It also flooded the event log so nothing else could be seen. Now: it tries each transceiver once per glitch, then — if no packet comes back (transmitter gone/out of range) — backs off to a slow once-a-second probe instead of storming, and re-arms instant failover the moment a real packet returns. Dead-link swaps no longer spam the log. Fast genuine failover between two good transceivers is unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.137-mac-burst-telemetry: The real fix for channels flashing to zero every ~10-15s with the sticks still (0.9.136 only moved the symptom). Root cause: the receiver was broadcasting its board ID to the transmitter continuously whenever you weren't actively moving a stick, and never sending telemetry — so the transmitter, starved of telemetry, hiccuped the link about every 10-15s (a brief RX-loss that flashed every channel to zero) and also never showed the RX version or the per-transceiver active-time counters until you wiggled a stick. Now the board ID is sent only as a short dense burst at the start of each connection (and re-sent on every reconnect), exactly like V1, then telemetry flows continuously. Result: rock-steady channels when not moving, and the version + counters appear immediately without touching the sticks. Note: the transmitter's 'Model IDs' identify screen now re-reads the ID on reconnect rather than continuously.
RXV2-0.9.136-failsafe-flash-fix: Fixes all channels briefly flashing to zero in the flight-controller (e.g. Rotorflight Configurator) every few seconds while the sticks are held still — a momentary false RXLOSS. The receiver was deciding 'link lost' from the last packet that carried channel data, but with the sticks still the transmitter sends only changed channels, so the gaps between changes (filled with parameter/no-change packets) made the link look dropped for an instant. Failsafe is now judged from the actual packet stream from the bound transmitter (which never stops while connected), so the channels stay rock-steady when you're not moving the sticks. Important for steady hovers.
RXV2-0.9.135-radio-timer-fix: Fixes the per-transceiver 'active time' counters on the TX screen sitting frozen at 0 on a solid link. The active radio's dwell time is now accrued continuously every loop (not via a live-delta that didn't land on a no-swap link), so one counter always ticks once per second while connected — matching V1.
RXV2-0.9.134-sim-wifi-top: Refines 0.9.133: instead of a separate button lower down, simulator mode now repurposes the existing top 'Fly now' button as 'Turn off WiFi — less interference' (same WiFi-off-until-reboot action, kept at the top where the Fly button lives). One control, one place, in both flying and sim use.
RXV2-0.9.133-sim-wifi-off: Simulator mode gains a 'Turn off WiFi' button (it only appears while in sim mode). Tapping it cuts WiFi to reduce radio interference while the simulator keeps running over USB — handy on a noisy bench, though not as critical as the Fly button before real flying. WiFi (and phone control) automatically comes back on the next power-cycle/reboot.
RXV2-0.9.132-update-bar: The firmware-update 'Installing…' screen now shows the same green progress bar as the simulator reboot screen (fills over ~30 s, snaps to full the moment the receiver is back) instead of a seconds counter, and its redundant Return-to-menu button is gone — it returns to the home screen by itself.
RXV2-0.9.131-reboot-bar: The 'Rebooting…' screen when starting/stopping simulator mode now shows a progress bar (fills over a few seconds, snaps to full the moment the receiver is back) instead of a seconds counter, and the now-redundant Return-to-menu button is gone — it returns to the home screen by itself.
RXV2-0.9.130-check-size: Fixes the update check failing ('network error') and the long pause entering simulator mode. The receiver was proxying the entire local + public manifests (~95 versions each, ~76 KB total) which choked it. Now the manifests are trimmed to the newest 12 versions, and the receiver skips any manifest that's still oversized — so the check stays small and fast. Rollback to recent versions is unaffected.
RXV2-0.9.129-no-back-btn: Removed the now-redundant 'Return to menu' button from the bottom of the pages — the floating 🏠 home button (top-left) does that from anywhere, no scrolling. Each page's Help (?) now reminds you the 🏠 button is the way back.
RXV2-0.9.128-btn-clearance: Every page now starts its content just below the floating Home/Help buttons, so the bigger buttons no longer overlap titles, cards or text at the top of any screen.
RXV2-0.9.127-bigger-btns: Made the floating Home (🏠) and Help (?) buttons bigger — easier to spot and tap.
RXV2-0.9.126-home-btn: Every page now has a fixed home button (🏠, top-left, mirroring the ? help button) that jumps straight back to the front menu — no more scrolling to the bottom to find Return to menu. Shown on all screens except the home page itself.
RXV2-0.9.125-check-retry: Makes the firmware check robust to a transient blip: it now retries once (after the receiver has had a moment to settle its WiFi, e.g. just after a reboot) before giving up. Fixes the spurious 'Network error talking to the receiver' on the firmware page and makes the 'Update now?' dialog appear reliably.
RXV2-0.9.124-update-prompt: When you open a receiver, it now checks for newer firmware straight away and, if there is some, pops an 'Update now?' dialog (installed vs available shown) instead of just a banner. Tap Update now and it downloads, flashes and reboots itself, then returns to the home screen — one tap, no firmware page needed. The banner remains as a tap-to-update fallback; Later dismisses it. (The check still defers while a transmitter link is live, so it never interrupts flying.)
RXV2-0.9.123-fly-bind-guards: Two home-screen fixes. 'Fly now' now disables WiFi directly — one tap, with a friendly confirm that also shows your live link status (it used to just open a page where you had to find a second button). 'Start Bind mode' is now guarded: if the receiver is already bound/connected it warns before erasing the bind and dropping the link (so you can't do it by accident); unbound, it still binds straight away.
RXV2-0.9.122-status-led: Adds support for an external status LED on the D4 pad: OFF = bound but no link, ON = connected & receiving, 2 Hz flash = binding. Only active when transceiver 3 is absent (D4 is radio 3's CE on triple-radio boards, so those are unaffected — auto-detected). LED is assumed wired pad->resistor->LED->GND (active-high); tell me if yours is inverted.
RXV2-0.9.121-help-per-sim: The ? help on the controls & views screen now matches the simulator you opened: neXt gets its own help (its keys, why there are no Select/Up/Down buttons, and the Mac Input-Monitoring steps), RealFlight keeps its full controls-and-views help.
RXV2-0.9.120-simple-look: Cleaner look everywhere: all the tiny technical small print (ch 12 - 833us, F3, Keypad +, ...) is gone from the controls and the key buttons — just clear labels now. RealFlight's key buttons are the same bigger size as neXt's. (The key assigned to each button is still shown in the editor.)
RXV2-0.9.119-next-clean: neXt's screen no longer shows the Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset buttons — they're RealFlight User-Interface bindings and do nothing in neXt. The neXt key buttons are bigger to use the space (and the page skips the now-pointless button polling, kinder to the radio). RealFlight's screen is unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.118-nice-confirm: The are-you-sure box for starting/leaving simulator mode is now a friendly colourful card in the app's own style (with a big green Yes and a Cancel), replacing the browser's grey utilitarian confirm dialog. Tap outside it to dismiss.
RXV2-0.9.117-prof-front: The simulator choice now lives ONLY on the home screen: the RealFlight / neXt switch has been removed from the controls & views screen, whose title now simply shows which simulator is active (e.g. 'neXt — controls & views'). Tapping a home button always opens with the right key set; to change simulator, return to the menu.
RXV2-0.9.116-reboot-ux: No more white screen when toggling simulator mode: the phone now shows 'Rebooting — please wait...' immediately (drawn before the toggle is even sent, so it cannot blank), counts the seconds, then returns to the home screen by itself — with a Return-to-menu button there throughout. And the home menu now has TWO simulator buttons — RealFlight and neXt — each opening the controls & views screen with that simulator's key set selected.
RXV2-0.9.115-return-fix: Sim-mode toggle (and every other reboot page) now reliably returns to the home screen: a Return-to-menu button is always shown (one tap recovers it — never close-and-reload again), polling starts sooner and waits longer, the redirect dodges stale caches, and coming back to a backgrounded tab re-checks immediately. Also the Simulator switch (RealFlight / neXt) above the camera buttons is now big and obvious with a 'Simulator:' label — it was too subtle to spot before.
RXV2-0.9.114-next-keys: The neXt profile now comes pre-filled with neXt 2.087's real keys (from its Settings -> Misc list): New model, Engine, Pause, Self level, Trainer, Piro trainer, Time scale, Set spawn, Prev model/scenery, Landing gear, flight Conditions 1-4, Mute, Music, Recorder, Screenshot, Chat, Menu. All editable per profile as before; anything you'd already saved for neXt is kept.
RXV2-0.9.113-sim-profiles: Two simulators, two key sets: new RealFlight / neXt chips above the camera buttons switch between separate view-key profiles, each remembered on the phone. RealFlight keeps its pre-filled keys (and your edits); neXt starts empty — select it and tap Edit view keys to add keys from neXt's keyboard list. Chosen deliberately over USB host auto-detection, which is unreliable (and wrong under a VM).
RXV2-0.9.112-mac-help: Help now covers using the simulator on a Mac (neXt etc.): quit the Keyboard Setup Assistant, and crucially enable your simulator in System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Input Monitoring (then restart it) — macOS hides the sticks from the sim until you do, because the device is part keyboard. Help-text only; no behaviour change.
RXV2-0.9.111-view-colours: Every camera/view button now has its own colour, so you can find a favourite by colour at a glance. Colours are fixed to each button slot (your favourite stays the same colour), and the editor shows each slot's colour dot.
RXV2-0.9.110-equal-pills: Select and Cancel are now each full-width — the same size as Reset; Up/Down triangles a touch smaller to make room.
RXV2-0.9.109-ctl-fill: Controls screen: all the buttons grow a little more to use the spare white space — wider/taller Up & Down triangles, taller Select/Cancel/Reset with larger text. Scroll behaviour unchanged.
RXV2-0.9.108-touch-fix: Scrolling fixed: a vertical swipe now scrolls the page even when it starts on the big Up/Down triangles (scrolling never fires them; a quick tap still does). Up/Down triangles made a bit smaller, Select/Cancel/Reset a bit bigger.
RXV2-0.9.107-big-ctl: Controls now FILL the first screen (huge Up/Down triangles + bigger Select/Cancel/Reset, with Reset full-width) so you can hit them without looking at the phone; scroll down for the views. Views expanded with RealFlight's other commands: Look at ground, Zoom reset, Follow/Pivot/Orbit cam, Next pit view, Zoom/Move mode, Kill engine, Flight failures, Screenshot, Record, Mute — all editable, and your earlier key edits are kept. Also fixes the Up/Down labels overlapping.
RXV2-0.9.106-ctl-size: Tuned the RealFlight controls & views screen: bigger controls — especially the Up/Down triangles — so you can hit Up/Down repeatedly while watching the sim on a TV across the room, with the camera/view buttons made a little smaller to balance. Cosmetic only.
RXV2-0.9.105-rf-ui: RealFlight controls and Views are now ONE home-menu item opening a single screen: controls up top (Select/Cancel/Reset as smaller ovals, Up/Down as up/down triangles you press & hold to repeat), the camera/view buttons below, then a darker 'Edit view keys' button. Cosmetic only — same buttons, channels, keys and behaviour.
RXV2-0.9.104-edit-btn: Views page: moved the Edit button down below the camera buttons so it no longer sits under the top-right ? Help button. Nothing else changed — same buttons, keys and mappings.
RXV2-0.9.103-rf-views: Views page defaults are now RealFlight 9.5's real View Commands (read from its Keyboard Commands dialog): Chase/Fixed/Nose cam = F3/F1/F2, Cockpit = F4, Cycle cam = C, Zoom in/out = keypad +/-, Windsock = Up arrow. Tap 'Reset to defaults' to load them; the editor still lets you map any key/combo to any RealFlight command.
RXV2-0.9.102-views-editor: The Views page now has an on-screen Edit button: set each button's label and pick its key from a friendly dropdown (Ctrl/Shift/Alt too), Save — stored on the phone, no re-flashing. So you can map the buttons to RealFlight's real view shortcuts yourself.
RXV2-0.9.101-keyboard: Sim mode is now a USB composite device: the existing gamepad PLUS a standard keyboard. New 'Views (camera)' phone page sends keyboard shortcuts (next view, zoom, cockpit/chase, etc.) to RealFlight — keycodes editable in the page. Gamepad report unchanged (a one-time RealFlight re-detect of the composite device aside). Keystrokes are non-blocking and don't affect the channel rate.
RXV2-0.9.100-reset-ch10: Swapped Reset and Select channels: Reset now on channel 10 (a switchable channel on the transmitter), Select on channel 14. Reset is the one you most want on a physical switch. Channels now: 10=Reset, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Select; ch9 still free for autorotation.
RXV2-0.9.99-tap-reliable: Makes the RealFlight-controls phone buttons more reliable: a tap now fires 3 times over ~180 ms (so an occasional dropped WiFi request no longer loses the press), and the button pulse is longer (250 ms) so the sim can't miss the edge. The firmware merges the repeats into one clean press — never a multi-fire.
RXV2-0.9.98-reset-ch14: Moved the RealFlight-controls Reset button from channel 9 to channel 14 (joystick button 6), leaving channel 9 free for RealFlight's helicopter autorotation. Channels now: 10=Select, 11=Cancel, 12=Up, 13=Down, 14=Reset. Page-only change; no re-calibration. You'll need to put the Reset switch on TX ch14 and re-bind Reset in RealFlight.
RXV2-0.9.97-usb-revert: Reverts the 0.9.96 non-blocking USB write — it halved the TX frame rate while flying the sim (≈200 vs 500 with sim off). The blocking write yields the CPU and paces the loop, which the radio link needs. Back to the proven behaviour. Keeps the 'RealFlight controls' rename and the return-to-home fix.
RXV2-0.9.96-ui-polish: Front-menu 'Sim controls' renamed to 'RealFlight controls' (those buttons are RealFlight's UI functions). After toggling simulator mode, the reboot page now waits for the receiver to be solidly back before returning to the home screen, instead of landing on a blank page. Also makes the USB sim write non-blocking so it can't stall the loop.
RXV2-0.9.95-loop-diag: Diagnostic build: adds loop_hz (main-loop iterations/sec) and loop_max_us (worst loop stall) to /api/state.json, to tell a CPU/servicing limit from an RF problem when chasing dropped frames. No functional change.
RXV2-0.9.94-wifi-quiet: Sim mode now runs WiFi at much lower power (8.5 dBm vs 19.5) so it stops desensitising the nRF24 receiver sitting right beside it — the cause of the short range and dropped frames when driving the sim (WiFi and the TX link share 2.4 GHz). Should markedly lift the frame rate and range. Normal mode keeps full WiFi reach. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.93-bind-restore: Reverts the 0.9.92 loop change (servicing the radio 3x per loop), which disturbed the timing-sensitive bind/hop handshake and stopped the transmitter binding. Back to the proven 0.9.91 radio servicing. Keeps the lighter Sim-controls polling. Proper fix (a dedicated radio core) to follow.
RXV2-0.9.92-link-fix: Fixes a reluctant / flaky TX link when a web page was open during sim use. The radio is now serviced before AND after the web server (and after the USB sim write), so a slow web request can no longer make the receiver miss an FHSS hop or ack. The Sim controls page also polls 3x more gently and pauses when hidden. No re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.91-menu-fit: Sim controls: the Return-to-menu button is now full-width but a normal height, so the five function buttons (Select/Up/Down/Cancel/Reset) grow taller to fill the screen. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.90-pad-menu: Sim controls tidy-up: all six buttons now exactly the same size, with a full-size 'Return to menu' button at the bottom (the tiny top link is gone). Up is pale blue and Down dark blue for quick contrast. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.89-big-pad: Sim controls is now one tall column of big, easy-to-hit targets filling the screen, in order Select · Up · Down · Cancel · Reset — Reset largest at the bottom, like the spacebar. Same colours and Up/Down auto-repeat. Page-only change; no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.88-sim-pad: Sim controls redesigned as a proper pad: big red Reset, green Select, amber Cancel, and a stacked ▲/▼ Up/Down rocker. Up and Down now AUTO-REPEAT — hold the on-screen button (or a TX switch on ch12/ch13) to scroll a menu continuously. Joystick descriptor unchanged (8 buttons), so no re-calibration.
RXV2-0.9.87-ui-buttons: Sim controls page now shows exactly RealFlight's 5 User Interface functions — Reset, Select, Cancel, Up, Down (ch9→Reset … ch13→Down) — instead of generic labels. The joystick is unchanged (still 8 HID buttons under the hood), so no re-calibration is needed.
RXV2-0.9.86-sim-buttons: Sim mode gains 8 function buttons on the USB joystick — fire them from the new 'Sim controls' phone page OR from your transmitter's switches on channels 9-16 (ch9→button1 … ch16→button8). Bind each to a sim function (reset, pause, view…) in your sim's controller setup, and control the sim with no keyboard. Adding buttons changes the joystick, so it needs one re-calibration in the sim.
RXV2-0.9.85-fresh-ui: Web pages are now sent no-store, so a freshly-updated UI appears immediately instead of the browser (iOS Safari especially) showing a stale cached copy — no hard-refresh needed.
RXV2-0.9.84-fs-auto: The receiver now derives its web-filesystem URL from the firmware URL when the page doesn't supply it, so it pulls its own web files on the next update even from a stale page — updating twice fully self-heals an out-of-date UI, no computer needed. Backups still preserved.
RXV2-0.9.83-fs-ota: OTA install now also flashes the matching web/data filesystem (and preserves your Rotorflight backups), so the web UI travels with the firmware on every update — no separate uploadfs needed. First release that ships a littlefs.bin.
RXV2-0.9.82-tx-happy: Firmware-update check no longer stalls the radio while the TX link is live (it was starving radioPoll and dropping the transmitter); shorter idle timeouts.
RXV2-0.9.81-wifi-heal: WiFi self-heals from AP-only — retries the home network every 20 s when it has saved credentials, instead of staying stranded. Plus a big SIMULATOR-MODE-ON home banner.
RXV2-0.9.80-sim-safe: Drive-simulator-over-USB now disables the flight-controller output (D6 stays silent) so a real model can't be flown from sim mode; default channel map shown as a tidy 1:1.
RXV2-0.9.79-usb-sim-remap: Adds the Remap-channels page for simulator mode (feed any of the 8 sim outputs from any received channel, with live bars).
RXV2-0.9.78-usb-sim: First release with Drive-simulator-over-USB: the receiver can present as a USB HID joystick for a PC flight sim, driven by the channels it receives — no separate dongle.
